Strong volume acceleration measured by OBV coupled with a rising ATR signals an expanding volatility regime; when the price is above the short‑term EMA the market is already trending upward, reducing the likelihood of false breakouts and improving risk‑reward. The same logic applied to the opposite side filters out weak pullbacks.

A sudden increase in OBV indicates a surge in buying volume that, when combined with a price above the short‑term EMA and an expanding ATR, signals a strong upward momentum; the ATR‑based stop and take‑profit scale risk and reward to current volatility, reducing slippage in volatile periods.

A trade is more likely to succeed when a sudden volume increase (OBV acceleration) occurs while the price is above a rising EMA and the market is in a high‑volatility regime (ATR expanding). This filters out weak or reverse moves, reducing large drawdowns caused by false breakouts.
